label: Six-ball trough and seventh release position
behavior: Six captive trough positions feed the right-hand release station (seventh contact). Coil 1 operates the separate 25-1240 lock-ball cam; coil 2 operates the 23-800 release plunger. Six subminiature contacts and one miniature release contact are physical, not optos. The table starts six balls in the stack, passing switches 14,13,12,11,10,9 to cvpmBallStack.InitSw after its zero entry-switch argument. Its coil-1 callback feeds a ball to BallRelease and coil 2 clears 15 and kicks toward the shooter. Keep the two actuators and the release contact separate. Ball movement, not a direct electrical coil-to-contact relation, changes the occupancy. A jam holds an occupied contact and prevents the expected transfer; table tuning is not a measured machine timing.

label: Shooter auto launch
behavior: Ball occupies shooter lane 16; output 3 pulses the 50V auto-launch kicker. The retained script uses the Shooter saucer and a variable kick force. TAG is a separate cabinet switch 62 even though the virtual table maps its plunger key to TAG. Do not add an unsourced manual-plunger switch.

label: Upper ring eject
behavior: The upper playfield's eject has a horizontal coil/plunger and a separate next-to-eject contact 28. Coil 4 kicks a ball from the table's sw28 saucer into the ring; 29 detects passage on the upper playfield. 29 is a ball-path sensor, not a coil position limit. No physical eject-home sensor is enumerated.

label: Right VUK to wire ramp
behavior: The right-side VUK captures a ball on 20; output 5 lifts it into the wire ramp. The local table uses sw20 for capture and sw20a for the kick. The coil chart calls this VUK and the switch chart calls 20 Super VUK; those names describe the same right-hand assembly. Spring return is mechanical; a pulse does not directly assert the ball contact.

label: Left and middle scoop subway / super VUK
behavior: Left/middle scoop balls pass the under-playfield trough contact 39 and arrive at the VUK's ball contact 40. Output 6 lifts the ball back to the playfield. The local script destroys the ball at sw39, pulses 39 for 200 ms, then adds a ball to the sw40 stack; that delay is a table approximation, not measured subway travel. The chart names coil 6 Super VUK but switch 40 Super VUK / VUK (Middle). Page 54 identifies the common left/middle assembly.

label: Lower left four-target D-A-E-D bank
behavior: Four individually latched down targets ordered top to bottom D,A,E,D. Each target holds its own contact until output 7 lifts/reset all four. The table maps cvpmDropTarget in that order and closes a contact when its target drops. Start with targets raised; reset pulses restore them. A bank that does not rise leaves contacts closed and should remain detectable as a fault.

label: Upper ring three-target WWF bank
behavior: Three individually latched drop targets ordered upper-playfield left, middle, right. Output 9 lifts the common reset bracket; contacts 30,31,32 follow the targets. The table's dtT InitDrop and SolDropUp preserve this order. The parts page's shaded two-target variants are not fitted to this game.

label: Rear panel ramp diverter
behavior: Rear-panel coil 32-1800 moves an armature/paddle against a 15 oz spring. No position switch is present in the complete assembly table or matrix. The local table's SolBackDiverter rotates its visual 0/40 degrees and a hidden collision flipper while enabled/disabled. Those angles and the hidden flipper pivot outside the playfield are table-owned; they are not physical coordinates or measured travel.

label: Upper playfield left diverter
behavior: 27-1500 coil, spring, plunger, crank arm and left shaft/paddle 515-6023-00 route the upper-left ring entry. No position sensor is enumerated. The table drives Flipper3 plus LeftDiverter at 0/-35 degrees with output 13. Preserve the output level and ball routing; do not interpret the script's flipper helper as an extra physical flipper.

label: Upper playfield right diverter
behavior: 27-1500 coil, spring, plunger, crank and right paddle/shaft 515-6024-00. The exact script ignores disabled callbacks, starts RightDivT on enabled callbacks, alternates a divstate flag, animates 0 to 45 degrees and back on successive enabled commands, and swaps TRDiv1/TRDiv2 collision walls. Initial script flag is false and TRDiv2 is dropped at startup. This proves the retained virtual routing contract; it does not establish physical home orientation, whether the real paddle is held or toggled, or physical travel time. Keep mechanism_behavior missing until an operating production assembly can be observed against output 22.

label: Four flippers on two solid-state boards
behavior: Two lower 22-1080 coils (500-5755-01 right / -02 left) and two upper 25-1800 coils (500-5820-01 right / -02 left). SSFB 1 serves lower and SSFB 2 upper, with 50V DC power and 8V AC hold supplies. The upper coil chart has no EOS; lower EOS is local hardware. PinMAME uses FLIP6364 without FLIP_SOL/EOS, copies host 84 to matrix 63 and 82 to 64 and fabricates 45/46 right and 47/48 left together while 23 is enabled. The ROM cannot consume the upper flipper-column bits. The exact table reads 46/48 and moves both same-side flippers together; independent physical staging and the power/hold waveforms are not represented by those synthetic pairs. No EOS simulation is needed by the emulated ROM.

label: Captive ball and TAG target banks
behavior: Two three-standup T-A-G banks (amber left, yellow right) qualify Collect Tag; a separate captive ball strikes switch 47. The script creates a captive ball once and binds its trigger separately from the six standups. This captive ball is additional to the six free trough balls and is never inserted into the trough stack.

label: Cabinet shaker motor
behavior: Cabinet shaker motor, PPB Q1/J8-11, no position sensor. Coil test names and drives output 16. The retained table comments out its shake callback, so that omission does not make the fitted motor unused. A recreation may provide the rumble effect from 16; strength and motor inertia are implementation-owned.

label: Three turbo bumpers and two slingshots
behavior: Three 500-5227-00 turbo bumpers and two 500-5226-00 slings. Switches 49/50/51 name left/bottom/right turbo; 19/27 name left/right slings. WWF's Cycling Coils names public 17/18/19 left/bottom/right turbo and 20/21 left/right sling. These are ROM-controlled PIA special outputs; PinMAME's per-game ssSw array is empty, so a recreation animates its local rubber/bumper physics separately and does not assume the emulator synthesizes a coil from a host closure.
